advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that setting `[code_health] analyzers=...` in TOML emits a deprecation warning on the `rebar` logger AND `load_config` does NOT raise AND the key is dropped (a cfg-warn analogue of test_warn_env_var_warns_not_errors).
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:762-764 shows the runtime path: `raise_or_warn_cfg_key(sect, tkey)` then `d.pop(tkey)` — the warn-and-drop behavior under test

tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py:141 `test_warn_env_var_warns_not_errors` exercises only env-kind (REBAR_PUSH); no analogous cfg-warn test exists (no matches for a cfg-warn TOML-key warn test)
tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py:47-59 only checks the key is accounted for by a tombstone NAME, not that the tombstone fires warn-and-continue

ABSENCE: previously `code_health.analyzers` was coerced via `_as_str_dict` (removed row); the new observable behavior — a set `[code_health] analyzers=...` must log a warning AND load must NOT raise AND the key is dropped — is untested, so a mis-wired cfg tombstone (wrong section.key) passes CI silently
advisory.finding: The new `code_health.analyzers` cfg-warn tombstone (which replaces the removed coercion so a still-set key WARNS-and-is-dropped instead of raising/being coerced) has no test asserting that runtime warn-and-continue behavior. The only warn-behavior test covers env-kind (REBAR_PUSH); there is no cfg-warn test, and the golden-surface guard only checks the tombstone name exists in the registry, not that it fires at config load.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/interfaces/contracts/test_tombstone_registry.py add a cfg-warn test: write a rebar.toml with `[code_health]\nanalyzers = { python = "lizard" }`, load config under caplog.at_level(WARNING, logger="rebar"), assert it does not raise, assert the warning names `code_health.analyzers`, and assert the resulting CodeHealthConfig has no such attribute / the key was dropped.
